significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that conditional backdoors generally create a measurable coupling between semantic/edit distance and activation distance—specifically, a "sharp discontinuity" and heavier-tailed "paraphrase-invariance violation" when an input crosses the trigger condition—making this a form-(iii) predictive relation rather than merely an existence claim. That relation would constrain expected activation geometry across trigger types and would provide a common explanation for attacks whose persistence and diversity are documented by Sleeper Agents (Hubinger et al., 2024) and the BackdoorLLM benchmark (Li et al., 2024). The claimed phenomenon is trigger-agnostic discrimination of backdoored models and inputs, while the proposed mechanism is a hidden conditional gate whose behavioral switch necessarily disrupts the local paraphrase manifold; together these are substantially more constraining than the topic's ordinary one-circuit/one-behavior hypothesis. A negative result would meaningfully rule out activation discontinuity as a necessary property of conditional backdoors, although terms such as "smooth" and "sharp" leave some quantitative indeterminacy; after topic substitution, generic mechanism-based LLM safety would not warrant this score, so the score rests on the specific cross-trigger geometric law.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "model-level screen" based on a "local Lipschitz/anomaly profile" and the "inference-time input flag" based on outlier status within a "paraphrase cloud." The former is ex ante because it can "screen suspicious models" before deployment, and the latter can flag a prompt before generation or release, giving auditors or deployment operators an action window rather than merely explaining a completed failure. After per-model recalibration, the conclusion would still predict the qualitative relation to recover—low-variance paraphrase neighborhoods for clean behavior and anomalous activation jumps when trigger conditions are crossed—although it provides no transferable numerical threshold and therefore falls short of a universal plug-and-play detector. The hypothesis asserts scope over "any conditional backdoor" and diverse trigger forms, with uptake by model auditors and deployers; deleting those specific handles and the paraphrase-discontinuity relation leaves only the broad safety topic, which would not retain this score.
